I used Booking.com to book this hotel for a High Level Delegation to travel to UNGA81 and this review is based on my own interaction with Staff and the reported interactions with the members of the delegation and staff as told to me. I would love for them to alledge review fraud and take action so I can trumpet to all who will hear just how entirely this particular branch of this hotel failed us. The stay was for the duration of one week for UN General Assembly High Level meetings from Sept 20-27

This entire experience was fraught with instances where their computer system failed them. Apparently that was not the only thing that failed them. Their elevator malfunctioned leaving one delegation member stranded on the elevator for 45 minutes. Without apology, the staff advised that if our delegate, who was their guest was unhappy with the fact that the elevator failed and they could not rectify the situation for 45 minutes leaving her in the elevator suspended for almost an hour, we were advised to raise the query with Booking.com who, according to them indemnified them totally from all liability.

There were multiple instances where their card reader could not read international credit cards. On one occasion, they locked a delegate member out of her room and demanded the full payment for her room for the entire duration of her stay although it appeared that they were debiting the cards attached to the booking on a daily basis. 

On the final day when they were to produce receipts, their system was down. And on all occasions when queries were raised they declared themselves indemnified against all liability because of booking.com.

I never let on that although I am Ambassador to the UN for the particular country that was ill-treated, I am also a lawyer and their understanding of how indemnity works couldn't be more incorrect.  Long story short, forego this hotel. They are totally not ready to accomodate international travellers. In words they will understand...they suck!
title: THIS HAS GOT TO BE THE WORST HILTON HOTEL IN THEIR ENTIRE CHAIN

text: In NY for the UN General Assembly (like everybody else this week). It's at the more standard end of the Hilton scale. One of those city hotels that people use for 2 nights max and move on. I was here for 8! Only serves breakfast, though you can get snacks at the bar and in the shop, which means once breakfast is over you really have to dine out. Breakfast is not cheap by European standards, with all the various taxes you are looking at $70 a head...so pop out to a diner. That said the rooms are clean, room service prompt and it serves as a good base, being just off Times Square and near the Metro (MTA). Staff are friendly and happy to help.
title: A good base for an NY stay.
